translations.text: Those who do improper things among us—this is how we bring shame on the good people among us who do good, we who do evil.
Oh, how clearly we show that we are lovers of sin!
Noah was righteous and innocent, living among those who had abandoned God.
Yet we ourselves sin in the midst of those who have left sin behind, to do [?]
Lot lived with people more wicked than anyone else. And
we live
For many among all the saints, down to Daniel and his companions, lived in the midst of godless people. They kept themselves holy and did not sin.
Yet we ourselves sin in the midst of those who love God. We gather together with them, and we all pronounce the name of God and his angels. We also speak about the saints.
We also speak and listen, we who are unworthy: “I appeal to the elders among you as a fellow elder and a witness to the sufferings of Christ.”

If someone tells us that we do not know God or his law, we become angry with him. Yet we ourselves do godless deeds. What, then, shall we say in the face of these words: “Everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him”?
Is not the tree [?]? Not only does it bend beneath its fruit, but it also carries it.
Is it not written, “Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire”?
If the saints and our fathers, the prophets and the apostles, and all the righteous said about themselves:

“Jews and Greeks, our solemn deeds have become a laughingstock.” And again: “O man, Jesus is the truth. Do not look at me, but at Jesus. Do not call anyone on earth your teacher. As for how I will act, you have no business with me. You are not slaves of people who bought you for a price. Jesus is the one who gave his blood; he is your Lord.” And again: “Perhaps some people, when they hear me, will say, ‘I will go out and plunder,’ for the teacher is like the one who gives encouragement. Perhaps you suspect that the person saying these things, if it overtakes him, will become even greedier and will take advantage of others. And you are not mistaken in saying these things.” Moreover, because there is someone who hates, and there are people who are always searching for something against those who speak the truth, he said: “We have said enough. We have spoken openly. Let whoever hates go on hating. Let whoever is distressed go on being distressed. For we will give an account to God, in the place where there is no profit or money to drive out the truth.” He said these things not only about us who are in the house of God. When he also saw that evil had increased on earth, especially oppression because of the love of money, instead of saying, “We will go to God as better or good people,” he said, “We will depart worse than when we came, for we did not come with possessions. Nor did we have sins or possessions then. But now the possessions will remain here, along with all the other empty desires. The sins, however, will go ahead of us, come with us, and follow behind us.” But who can speak of the perfection of that man of God, and of all his words, which contain neither hypocrisy nor an effort to please oppressive people, any pagan, any heresy, or anyone who is not upright?

“For we will give an account to God, in the place where there is no profit or money to drive out the truth.” He said these things not only about us who are in the house of God. When he also saw that evil had increased on earth, especially oppression because of the love of money, instead of saying, “We will go to God as better or good people,” he said, “We will depart worse than when we came, for we did not come with possessions. Nor did we have sins or possessions then. But now the possessions will remain here, along with all the other empty desires. The sins, however, will go ahead of us, come with us, and follow behind us.”

150. When we receive the title of ruler and authority, each according to his kind, and we all boast of the high positions belonging to God and of his holy places, we do not know what will confront us when we give God an account of all our deeds. If only we would not suffer even greater shame and grief on that day! For we will say that we regret it, and we will weep in the place where [?] friendships [?] we [?] toward nothingness.
There is a person who rejoices when he receives necessary goods entrusted to him, and who gives them back with confidence to the person who entrusted them to him when that person asks him for them.

And there is a person who rejoices when he reaches out to receive what has been entrusted to him [?] again, for he becomes gloomy and grieves. He is also afraid because he has not safeguarded what was put into his hands. Instead, they drag him to the places of judgment, covered in shame and afraid, and also full of turmoil, not thinking of escaping. Understand, rather, these things that you hear, O man who looks forward to the place of judgment in heaven. And I too understand what this person who reveals things worth saying is saying, if I too take care to stand before the judgment seat of Christ. Not everyone is recognized as trustworthy at the time of receiving. Rather, the real test is the time of giving back what you received and proving yourself faithful by returning it to the person who gave it to you, with nothing missing. A person will inquire and test who is trustworthy enough to have earthly goods entrusted to him, although they will perish. And there is a person who examines him before he receives them, to see whether he will safeguard what has been put into his hands. Will it happen, then, that those who receive high positions from God fail to examine themselves and those who receive the title through them, and fail to assess what they are or what kind they are, along with their other deeds? How will someone say, '[?] exists [?] establish [?] all of them [?],' saying:
Rather, these things that you hear, O man.

Not everyone is recognized as trustworthy at the time of receiving. Rather, the real test is the time of giving back what you received and proving yourself faithful by returning it to the person who gave it to you, with nothing missing.

A person will inquire and test who is trustworthy enough to have earthly goods entrusted to him, although they will perish. And there is a person who examines him before he receives them, to see whether he will safeguard what has been put into his hands. Will it happen, then, that those who receive high positions from God fail to examine themselves and those who receive the title through them, and fail to assess what they are or what kind they are, along with their other deeds?
How will someone say, '[?] exists [?] establish [?] all of them [?],' saying:
Those who do those abominable deeds in the holy places are themselves traitors, thieves, and apostates.
What use are many lamps placed on lampstands if they do not burn because they are no good?
Likewise, that of the holy and faithful people who live in it.
A person who is of no use to himself and does not benefit himself—how will he be useful for a necessary task? Or is there an honored title that will benefit him? Judas was of no use to himself alone.
For a necessary task.
That apostate, while the Lord says, 'If a person gains the whole world and loses his soul,'
What will he give in exchange for his soul?
To give himself over to a trap of the devil.

Concerning money: if only, then, gold had never existed! Yet we also receive it gladly when God gives it to us for a need. But to bear that judgment because of it is lawlessness. If only gold had never existed, and they would not have sold the righteous person for silver, and [?].
If only gold had never existed, and they would have handed over the righteous person
at all times, and to plant.
Or to bring people in to them who will recognize the favor of the one who honored them.

[?] ship watches the mouse’s [?], so that we too may guard our hearts with every precaution, as it is written, against every evil thing that creeps into them or drips thoughts into them that destroy the hearts and souls of the people who accept them. For it was because of these things that they said, “They committed sexual immorality in the thoughts of their hearts.” These are the people whom the fall follows, as it is written, “Evil thoughts come before the fall.” It was because of these things that they said, “A lying spirit stood up and dripped wine and strong drink for you.” For through these things people of this kind come out to wage war against one another with these weapons of combat: jealousy, hatred, slander, insults, taunts, and things like these.

This is how Satan stirs up thoughts of many evils against one another in their hearts, until they make themselves liable to God’s judgment. For those whom he has made enemies of true righteousness in these ways are beyond counting, through a love that is mixed with jealousy and hatred. This is how we will be put to shame on the day when God judges people’s secrets. How will we hide our jealousy and our hatred for one another on that day? Who can raise a club against his neighbor—let alone a sword or a spear—without being seen? Yet who would think of us, or who would accuse us of stabbing one another with all these things, when they see how we speak to one another with every peaceful word, while hostility is in our hearts?

It is better not to ask after one another’s welfare, when there is wickedness in our hearts, than to ask with hypocrisy and false love. Do not ask, “Are you well?” or “Are you making progress in goodness?” Nor should you rejoice because you have heard about the things you want to happen to me. Do not say, “May he live a long time,” and then rejoice when you hear that he has died. What will this human honor do for us? Let us be ashamed before these words: “The Lord knows people’s thoughts, that they are empty.”

I am not coming into your hands because I am afraid or ashamed for you to learn that there are evil things in my heart against you. Nor are you coming into my hands because you are afraid or ashamed for me to hear that you speak evil against me. Rather, we are coming into God’s hands. We are not blessed merely because we bear a name while we are full of malice against one another. Rather, we are blessed if the Savior Jesus rescues us from Satan’s evil, this malicious deceit [?] in a person’s heart against his neighbor.

We sit at one table. I eat bread with you; your hand is in the dish with mine. We live together in the holy places. You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place Christ’s body in your hand; you draw his blood for me. Yet our hearts are full of evil against one another, and we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came upon those before us who became entangled in such evils. Were these things written in vain? Did they not know that many people would walk in God’s house at every time, while their hearts were not upright toward one another?

Whoever wants to know about evils like these and understand their repayment, look: they are written in the Psalms, which say of the people who committed them, “May death come upon them; may they go down alive into the underworld.” But do not twist what we are saying. For the holy people in God’s house who are grieved and find fault with those who do evil among them, to the point of regarding them as enemies, are one thing; those whose hearts are full of malice and hostility toward one another are another.

These words were not written in vain, or only about those who walked in God’s house in the beginning while their hearts were not upright toward one another, or about Judas alone: “The one who eats my bread has raised his heel against me,” or “He used to eat meals with me,” and the other things like these. Rather, they were written about those who would walk deceitfully in the holy places at every time, whose hearts were not upright with God, and whose hearts were not upright with one another.

Where is Judas now? He is in the underworld. Why? Because of theft and betrayal. His hand was in the dish with God, while he was ready to betray him. But let us fear Gehenna and be ashamed of ourselves, we who have received the name of God’s greatness. Let us keep ourselves holy, away from Judas’s deeds in God’s house. For that man committed these still greater evils: it was after he received the bread that Satan entered him. This great wrath justly came upon him in keeping with the wickedness of his deeds, because, instead of being cleansed of Satan by receiving some of the bread that the Lord broke and gave him, Satan entered him still further. This is how quickly he crossed over to the other side: instead of being an apostle, he became a devil.

You see that anyone who makes room for the unclean spirit within himself, after receiving grace, after receiving the name, after putting on the habit, will go on to commit many evils. Or did we not leave the house of our worldly life in order not to sin? And where will these deeds of malice, violence, thorns, and thistles come from to entangle us? Or will we become entangled in them through our foolishness and our negligence, which have made bitter things sweet to us? I am speaking of defilements, impurities, and sexual immoralities of every kind, things that are very far removed from the rules of honorable marriage and foreign to the undefiled marriage bed; and of jealousies, hatreds, slanders, excessive greed [?], favoritism in judgment, and all the other things with which we have filled God’s places. They are traps and nets for us, and stones and pits, so that we become entangled in them, stumble over them, and fall into them.

Who else is responsible for separating what is holy from what is defiled, and what is evil from what is good, as the person in God’s house is? For those who desire goodness will do what they see us doing; and those who do evil will do what they see us doing, and will do still more.

The unclean is not merely a defiled person who is separated from a holy person. Nor is what is defiled merely an animal unsuitable for offering as a sacrifice to the Lord, which is separated from what is clean according to the commandments. Rather, every evil, from crooked judgments down to hypocrisy, is unclean. Anyone who touches these things—that is, does them—will become unclean before God if he does not withdraw from them, just as every sin is an impurity in the eyes of those who truly belong to God.

This is how unjust judges are called “unclean,” because of their unclean deeds, and upright judges are called “clean,” because of their righteous deeds and their true judgments. Likewise, a person who humiliates a good person while honoring an evil person, and insults a righteous person in the presence of an ungodly person, has an unclean heart within him. Above all, he is like someone who blocks the mouth of a spring of water. Who will say that it is not so, except someone who has within him what God detests: pride, as it is written in the Gospel?

Or will we entertain these proud thoughts, I saying, “Are you really the one who will guide me?” and you saying, “Is this really the one who will teach me?” Yet we have not mourned over our sins, so that God will not cast us away from him on the day of our need. Or are these not people to whom he will say at that time, “Go away from me,” or “I do not know who you are”?

What will we say at that time? Will we say, “In your name we received positions of authority or high rank. In your name we clothed ourselves in habits. In your name we lived in your holy places. In your name we read the Scriptures”? These people too will say, “In your name we prophesied, and in your name we drove out demons, and in your name we performed many miracles.” But these things will be of no benefit. Why? Did they neglect the deeds? If he will say to these people, “Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire,” because they did not do the things he told them, then how much more woe is there for us, because we are ruining essential deeds, namely God’s judgments and what is right!

On the day when God will judge people's secrets, how will we hide our envy and our hatred toward one another on that day? Who will raise a club against his neighbor—let us call it a sword or a spear—without it being seen?

[?] not into your hands, because I am afraid or ashamed for you to know that there are evil thoughts in my heart toward you. Nor are you coming into my hands, because you are afraid or ashamed for me to hear that you speak evil against me. But we are coming into God's hands. We are not blessed merely because we bear a name while we are full of malice toward one another. Rather, we are blessed if the Savior Jesus rescues us from Satan's evil, this deceit of [?] that is in a person's heart toward his neighbor. We sit at the same table. I eat bread with you; your hand is in the bowl with mine. We live together in the holy places. You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place Christ's body in your hands, and you give me his blood to drink. Our hearts are full of evil toward one another, and we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came upon those before us who were engulfed in evils like these. Were these things written down for nothing?
No, for many will walk at all times.
He is in Hades. Why? Because of theft and betrayal. His hand is in the bowl with God, while he is ready to betray him.
And
It is not only an unclean person who is separated from a holy person.
Nor is it only an unclean thing, unsuitable to be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord, that is separated from what is clean, according to the commandments.

With these acts of arrogance, I say, 'Are you the one who will guide me?' and you say, 'Is this the one who will teach me?' Yet we have not mourned over our sins so that God will not cast us away from him on the day of our distress. Or are these not also people to whom he will say at that time, 'Go away from me,' or, 'I do not know who you are'? What will we say at that time? Will we say, 'In your name we received offices or positions of authority. In your name we clothed ourselves in robes. In your name we lived in your holy places. In your name we read the Scriptures'?
Into the fire forever, because they did not do what he said. Then how much greater is our woe, since we destroy essential works, namely God's ordinances and what is right!

And the work of his hands—I mean each of our bodies—just as he made the members of Christ into the members of a prostitute through every devilish deed. But I will state this differently and explain it as a sign of the wrath that will come upon everyone who oppresses the poor. For if Jesus, when he comes, will say to those who did not feed him when he was hungry, did not give him drink when he was thirsty, and did not clothe him when he was naked, ‘Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire,’ then how much more will he curse those who plundered the houses of the poor and made them miserable, robbing them and taking the fruits of their labor, though they have no claim against them? He will rightly say to them, ‘Even if you did not give them food or clothing, why do you also take away the bread they have? Why do you leave them naked, stripped even of the clothing they are wearing?’ Someone who hates his brother has been compared to a murderer. It was because of this deed that the Lord God cast Cain out of his presence. And it is astonishing that we are not afraid when we hate one another, although the scripture says, ‘The father of a person who seeks wisdom will rejoice.’ If we hear that our children, or those who follow us in rank, though not in our deeds, have spoken words of God or done good deeds, we are distressed because we do not want anyone to say, ‘Someone else has done good things.’ Instead, we say, ‘There is no one equal to us.’ This is what gives rise to every kind of envy. Because of this, Cain rose against Abel and killed him. Because of this, they sold Joseph as a slave. Because of this, the Jews opposed what Paul was saying,

blaspheming. It is not surprising if Christians suffer at the hands of pagans or heretics because they envy them, just as the Philistines caused Isaac suffering because they envied him, and just as all the people of God have endured every kind of distress from the beginning until now because of all the godless people. But it is all the more astonishing that we envy one another, cause one another suffering, and hand one another over to death, although we have one and the same God. There is another thing that harms fathers and brings ruin upon children: those in authority honor people so that they will follow them, or appoint them to necessary tasks in God's service, although they hear about and know their evil deeds; and disobedient children and every undisciplined person hate those who tell them the truth.
because of all the godless people. But it is all the more astonishing that we envy one another, cause one another suffering, and hand one another over to death, although we have one and the same God.
And he killed them in his anger because they did not stop.
Not.

There are things that, if a person does not vow to do them, he incurs no sin. For the Lord said, ‘Let whoever is able to bear it bear it.’ But if he vows to do them and does not do them, woe to him! These are: remaining a virgin, taking up your cross to follow God, serving as a priest in his house, and becoming a monk. Therefore, whoever falls away from these things or turns back from them has himself denied, and has become a pillar of salt like Lot's wife—that is, a person with no wisdom in him. If we say, ‘These words contend against us,’
Even if they [?]

Nor would he himself have laid traps in the corners, in the streets, and around your house. You showed him the ways to come in and go out deceitfully. You hid him in your heart, your soul, and your mind, like a woman who hides her adulterous lover in the storerooms and corners of her house. You brought him to the place where your wealth was hidden. You pointed it out to him.

Search, you foolish virgin! Look through all your belongings, so that you may discover what he has not taken from the things that belong to you. Your purity is your great wealth. Your prayer is the bracelet and the rings of every kind on your hands and fingers. Your walking in freedom is the anklet on your feet. Your obedience is the earring in your ears. Your humility is the ring and bronze chain around your neck. Your knowledge is the ornament on your head or around your forehead. Your fasts are the bridles of your body. Your meditations on the word of God are the covering for your feet. Your good deeds are the fine clothes you usually wear. Your grace is the ointment and oil with which you usually anoint yourself and which you put on your head. Your truth is the [?] that you tie on. Your wisdom is the veil with which you cover yourself.

Which of these and the other things has he not taken from you—all of them, down to the eye paint? He poured it out of its containers and took it: your modesty, or the wholesome shame in your eyes.

That woman said to her brother, “I will take hold of you and bring you into my mother's house, into the chamber of the woman who conceived me.” Just as the true virgin now preserves all her wealth in the good deeds she has done in her strength, praying that Jesus and his Spirit may dwell in her, you took hold of an enemy and brought him into your house and your chamber. You welcomed the defiled and unclean spirit, but turned away from the holy and beloved one, the good Spirit—not because he is unable to save you, but because he handed you over to the one who hates you.

For you loved strangers and followed them. You loved those who sleep with you and increased your sexual immorality with them. You multiplied those who were alien to you, so that they would dwell in your house with you. I am speaking of the spirit of wickedness and the world rulers of darkness, and also the ungodly people who have entered into this same union with you, and you with them, you wretched soul! But your God and your Lord Jesus—do not abandon him.

You multiplied those who were alien to you, so that they would dwell in your house with you. I am speaking of the spirit of wickedness and the world rulers of darkness, and also the ungodly people who have entered into this same union with you, and you with them, you wretched soul!

[?] in their hearts and in their thoughts, as it is written: “He himself, when he saw you, forgot him [?]. And do not be afraid of him. He himself will declare his righteousness, and the wind will carry you away, together with all those attached to you in falsehood, and their deeds and their gold and silver. A wind will scatter them.”

So enough of us remaining in these deeds through which we stir up God's anger and wrath against us! How long, then, will we keep speaking to God hypocritically and stretching out our hands dishonestly before the one from whom the ugliness of our deeds is not hidden? We see these troubles upon the earth because of our acts of violence and all the things that none of us wants done to himself, yet we do them to one another.

“Remove the sins, and I will remove the sufferings, scourges, and afflictions from you,” says this voice, which declares: “Remove these evils from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness.” We see that we are bringing shame upon ourselves and defiling ourselves, together with our other good deeds. Who can pollute or defile the Lord's ordinances without first having polluted himself and defiled his deeds?

It is impossible for me to say anything without having to give an account for it. That is why I tell you: There is someone reading the Scriptures or singing psalms, and in heaven they say of him, “He deserves to have his mouth shut.” There is someone in the holy places, clothed, moreover, with the honored name, and in heaven they say of him, “The enemy of God's houses, who deserves to have the habit he is wearing torn apart.” There is someone going up to the altar and receiving the Lord's body and blood, and in heaven they say of him, “He deserves to have his hands and feet cut off.” There is a man, there is a woman, whom people on earth think of as lights in every kind of purity, and in heaven they say of them, “Look, people who are unclean in everything!”

There will certainly be a judgment between those who hear these words with sighs and tears and those who hear them with resentment and grumbling—even if they do not hate the one who rebukes them. What will this name and this habit do for us while we remain in these improper deeds? It is the word spoken by the prophet that will make us rich: “Let the coward become a warrior. Let the one who has no strength say, ‘I am strong.’”

With whom should the coward become a warrior? Or in what should he become strong? Let him fight for the truth and for God's judgments. Let him fight against sin. Let him become strong and resist empty glory, hypocrisy, favoritism, and fear of people's disapproval—especially that of wealthy oppressors and godless pagans.

The person who does not pay attention to his sins when he hears these words is the person who does not think about his end and the hour of his distress. The person who finds fault with the one who says these things is the person whose inward thoughts have been covered over by wickedness and impiety, as it is written. Everything from which we gain no benefit at the time of our distress is a loss to our soul.

In what have those who have come a great distance to this place become wiser, when they come to inquire or to obtain a judgment concerning possessions that have been stolen? A person whose work is to remove specks from people's eyes when they impair their sight—how is it not foolishness on his part if he removes the specks but leaves the beams in them?

I say this because, if I am here exposing people for having stolen possessions, or passing judgment on them, why should I not expose them for having been stolen by sin, pass judgment on them, and show them the places where the enemy has hidden them—that is, pollution, defilement, and every sin? The duty of this place is that we should benefit our soul, which the whole world is not worth.

Do not let anyone come to me about something of that kind. I am not someone of that kind. If there is someone you know who understands the things you are seeking, like the prophets and apostles, go to those people—but only if they themselves know that they will know the things about which you will go to them. Yet if you do go to them, you will not find mercy before God because of those things.

Brothers, it is not the world that has filled us with error; rather, it is we who have filled it. Therefore, it is time to become wise. Do not let anyone make fools of you, for there are many deceivers who make fools of many people through these practices. No one who fears God will speak words of this kind, even if they truly know.

The great prophet Moses was in the midst of the darkness and the cloud, with God speaking to him, so that nothing was hidden from him. Yet he never spoke words of this kind, nor did any of the other saints: “Go to such-and-such a place, and you will find possessions that have been stolen,” or, “Who took them?” That is what those who deceive many people nowadays say, though they know nothing. Instead, they said, “Every matter will be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses,” or that the stolen goods should be found in the possession of those who took them. Concerning the end of every dispute, he said, “An oath before God shall be between them.”

If Samuel said to Saul, “The donkeys have been found,” what does this matter have to do with the things you are saying? Saying who stole possessions and saying that they have been found are two different things. Is not saying, “They have been found,” a matter of peace? Is that the same as saying, “Look, they are in such-and-such a place,” or, “So-and-so took them,” as those who now stir you up to hostilities and other troubles do? You turn the houses of those whom they have identified to you by saying, “They are the ones who took them,” upside down, gaining nothing except falsehood, fighting, and hatred toward one another.

But since we have spoken what is sufficient, and have heard what is sufficient, I will leave these things. May the God of all compassion make us worthy of these two things, so that we may share in their entirety: that he protect the innocent among his people and that he also set us sinners straight, freeing us from every lawlessness. May he not hide his face from us from today onward, from the day when we resolved in our hearts to keep his words. For we too will hear this encouragement through this voice, like these words at this time:

“I will take you out of the nations and gather you from all the earth. I will bring you into your land and sprinkle pure water upon you”—that is, the perfect word of the Scriptures—“and you will be cleansed from all your impurities and from all your idols, and I will purify you.”

And again: “I establish a covenant of peace with them, and it shall be a covenant for them. I will settle them and multiply them, and place my sanctuary among them forever. My dwelling shall be over them.”

And again: “I will restore Jacob from captivity, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel.”

And again: “From this time onward I will no longer leave them in that place”—he is speaking of the land of their enemies—“and I will not hide my face from them, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, says Adonai, the Lord.”

I have said these things knowing that you wish to hear them. Indeed, I remember how I saw your tears flowing over your cheeks when this least of men spoke in this way: “We go up onto the seat or the throne to read to those who listen to God's word in his churches—or is it rather into pits that we descend?”

And again: “What wisdom does a shepherd have if he draws water and gives a flock of sheep something to drink, but does not himself drink a measure that belongs to him? Or if someone has lit many lamps in other people's houses, but does not light his own in his chamber?” And because you are wise and have understood [?].

Having done them for him, while we ourselves do them to one another. Remove the sins from there, and I will remove the sufferings, the scourges, and the afflictions from you. This voice said, “Remove these evil things from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness, so that we may see and reproach ourselves.”
For they are lights in every kind of purity, while it is said of them in heaven, “Look, they are impure in everything.”
And greed spreads a covering over the thoughts within his heart, as it is written: “Everything that does not benefit us in the time of our need is harmful to our souls.”
But if they recognized themselves, they would know what you are going to them about.
Because they have found glory. What does this matter have to do with the things you are saying?

And I will gather you from the whole earth and bring you into your land. I will sprinkle pure water upon you—that is, the perfect word of the Scriptures—and you will be cleansed of all your impurities and all your idols, and I will purify you. And again: “I establish a covenant of peace with them, and it will be a covenant for them. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever, and my dwelling will be over them.”
Or the throne, reading aloud to those who listen to the word of God.

For I call the reader’s soul the well, and his heart the storeroom, and the words the lamps and the waters, and the people the sheep, and the Scriptures the cisterns, and good deeds the high places, and evil deeds the pits. This is how you all dug with your tears, as we wept and reflected on our sins and our acts of ignorance.

An address before a very large number of clergy—priests and deacons—and other fathers of monasteries, and other monks who had come with them, making a great crowd. For all of them had come to see him and to hear words of God from him. Some of them had come to plead their cases, distressed and hostile toward one another over evil deeds, even thefts. For he had considered it necessary not to let them speak about the things they had come for until the next day, wanting silence to prevail so that those who loved instruction could hear what God would give. When he finished speaking on Sunday evening, as was his custom, those people left without bringing up at all the matters they had come for. For they had been ashamed, because they were being rebuked through these words, which are as follows:

Christ. Those who do those abominable deeds in the holy places are themselves traitors, thieves, and apostates. What use are many lamps placed on lampstands if they do not burn because they are defective, especially when they have been lit many times? The true word [?] tells us that nothing good will happen to people who conduct themselves deceitfully in the house of God. But for the holy and faithful people who dwell in it, their good deeds are to be seen, and they are to shine in the holy places. If someone is of no use to himself and does not benefit himself, how will he be useful for a necessary task? Or will an honored name benefit him? Judas was of no use to himself, nor was he of any use to the apostleship. What he gained was theft and betrayal. That apostate not only heard the Lord say, “If a person gains the whole world but harms his soul, what will he give in exchange for his soul?” He also heard him say, “One of you will betray me,” yet he was neither ashamed nor took pity on himself. He lost himself for thirty pieces of silver. He harmed himself, and he also lost the money.

Judas was no benefit to himself, nor was he any benefit to the apostleship. What he gained was theft and betrayal. That apostate not only heard the Lord say, “If a person gains the whole world but loses his soul, what will he give in exchange for his soul?” He also heard him say, “One of you will betray me.” Yet he was neither ashamed nor sorry for himself. He lost himself for thirty pieces of silver. He lost himself, and he also lost the money.

If we say, “If a person of whom the whole world is not worthy is going to put himself into a trap of the devil for money, then would that gold did not exist!”—nevertheless, we receive it with joy when God gives it to us for a need. But to incur that judgment because of it is lawlessness.
Would that gold did not exist, and that they would not sell the righteous person for silver! And [?]
This is how he showed patience when he spoke to them: “Why did you eat from this tree, the only one about which I told you not to eat from it?”

Eve said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.” But Adam said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.” And in this way he rebuked them, but he cursed the serpent.

But where will we go from the presence of God, since we act unjustly, commit adultery, seize things that are not ours, steal, lie, swear falsely, and commit all the other evils by which we provoke him to anger?

Adam and Eve quickly recognized the shame of the offense they had committed, and they did not take long to realize that they were naked. So they looked for a covering. They stitched fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths, for they were frightened and hid.

But we, who persist in our sins at all times, have not recognized the shame of our sins. Nor have we realized that we are stripped of the glory that clothed us before we sinned. So we do not concern ourselves with accepting commandments and doing the deeds commanded to us in the Scriptures, so that we may cover our disgrace.

If a barbarian invades a land or a district, where will its inhabitants flee to be safe, except to fortified cities? But if they take control of the strongholds, where will the inhabitants go? Perhaps those who are able will flee up into the mountains and be safe.

Likewise, if Satan attacks souls to deceive them and kill them through evil, to whom will they flee except those in positions of authority in the house of God, so that these may teach them the practices of warfare and the weapons of battle, and they may overcome sin? But if we are the first to grow weak or fall into evil when the enemy places stumbling blocks at our feet, where will the people go? Or who will help them?
But if we are the first to grow weak or fall into evil when the enemy places stumbling blocks at our feet, where will the people go?

Perhaps those who understand will lift their eyes to the mountains, as it is written—that is, they will resolve in their hearts to keep the words of the Scriptures, and they will see where their help comes from, and that it comes to them from the Lord who made heaven and earth.
If sailors attend to bailing or pouring out the water that crashes onto the ship through the waves or pours into it, then [?] safety.

A ship keeps watch against the rat’s gnawing [?], so that we too, with every precaution, may guard our hearts, as it is written, against every evil thing that leaps into them or pours into them thoughts that destroy the hearts and souls of the people who accept them. For it was because of these things that they said, “They committed sexual immorality in the thoughts of their hearts.” These are the things that destruction follows, as it is written: “Evil thoughts precede destruction.” It was because of these things that they said, “A lying spirit stood up and prophesied to you of wine and strong drink.” For through these things people of this kind come out to wage war against one another with these weapons of conflict: jealousy, hatred, slander, insults, resentment, and things like them. This is how Satan brings into them many dark thoughts against one another, until they make themselves liable to God’s judgment. For countless are those whom he has made enemies of true righteousness in these ways, with a love mixed with jealousy and hatred.

This is how we will be put to shame on the day when God judges people’s hidden things. How will we hide our jealousy and our hatred toward one another on that day? Who can raise a staff against his neighbor—not to mention a sword or a spear—without being seen? But as for us, who will suspect, or who will accuse us of stabbing one another with all these things, when they see how we speak to one another with every peaceful word, while hostility is in our hearts? It is better not to ask after one another’s well-being, with no wickedness in our hearts, than to ask hypocritically and with a false love. Do not ask, “Are you well?” or, “Are you making progress in goodness?” And do not rejoice because you have heard that the things you want to happen to me have happened. Do not say, “May he live a long time,” and then rejoice because you have heard that he has died.

What will this human glory do for us? Let us be ashamed before these words: “The Lord knows people’s thoughts, that they are empty.” I am not going to fall into your hands, so that I should be afraid or ashamed for you to learn that there are evil things in my heart against you. Nor are you going to fall into my hands, so that you should be afraid or ashamed for me to hear that you speak evil against me. Rather, we are going to fall into God’s hands. We are not blessed because we bear a name while being full of malice toward one another. Rather, we are blessed if the Savior Jesus delivers us from Satan’s evil, the deceit of [?] that is in a person’s heart against his neighbor.

We sit at a single table. I eat bread with you. Your hand is in the bowl with mine. We live together in the holy places. You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place Christ’s body in your hand; you pour out his blood for me. Yet our hearts are full of evil against one another, and we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came upon those before us who became entangled in evil things of this kind. Were these things written for nothing? Did they not know that many people in every age would walk in God’s house without their hearts being upright toward one another?

Whoever wants to know these evil things and understand their repayment, look: they are written in the Psalms, which say of the people who committed them, “Let death come upon them; let them go down alive into Hades.” But do not distort what we are saying. For the holy people in God’s house who are grieved and find fault with those who do evil among them, so that they count them as enemies, are one thing; those whose hearts are full of malice and hostility toward one another for no reason are another. These words were not written only about those who walked in God’s house in earlier times without their hearts being upright toward one another, or about Judas alone: “The one who eats my bread with me has raised his heel against me,” or, “He used to eat meals with me,” and the other things like these. Rather, they were written about those who would walk deceitfully in the holy places in every age, without their hearts being upright toward God and without their hearts being upright toward one another.

Where is Judas now? Why is he in Hades? Because of theft and betrayal. His hand was in the bowl with God, while he was preparing to betray him. But let us fear Gehenna and be ashamed before ourselves—we who have received the name of greatness before God—and let us keep ourselves holy, free from Judas’s deeds in God’s house. For that man committed these greater evils because it was after he received the bread that Satan entered him. That great wrath rightly came upon him in proportion to the wickedness of his deeds, because, instead of being cleansed of Satan by receiving some of the bread that the Lord broke and gave him, Satan entered him all the more. This is how he quickly crossed over to the other side: instead of being an apostle, he became a devil.

You see that whoever makes room within himself for the unclean spirit after receiving grace, after receiving the name, after putting on the habit, will undertake many evil things. Did we not leave the house of our worldly life in order not to sin? And where else will these deeds of darkness, these thorns, brambles, and reeds, come from to entangle us? Or will we become entangled in them through our foolishness and our negligence, which have made bitter things sweet to us? I am speaking of defilements, impurities, and sexual immoralities of every kind, which are very far removed from the rules of honorable marriage and foreign to the undefiled marriage bed; and of jealousies, hatreds, slanders, greed, partiality in judgment, and all the other things with which we have filled God’s places. They become snares and nets for us, and stones and pits in which we become entangled, against which we stumble, and into which we fall.

Who else has as much responsibility to distinguish the holy from the defiled, and the evil from the good, as the person in God’s house? For those who desire goodness will do things in the way they see us do them; and those who do evil will do things in the way they see us do them, and will go still further. The unclean is not only a defiled person who is separated from the holy person. Nor is the defiled only an animal that is unfit to be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord and is separated from the clean according to the commandments. Rather, every evil thing, from crooked judgments down to hypocrisy, is unclean. Whoever touches these things—that is, does them—will be unclean before God if he does not withdraw from them, just as every sin is an impurity in the sight of those who truly, truly belong to God.

This is how unjust judges are called “unclean” because of their unclean deeds, and upright judges are called “clean” because of their righteous deeds and their true judgments. Likewise, a person who demeans a good person, honors an evil person, and insults a righteous person in front of an ungodly person has an unclean heart within him, especially since he is like someone who blocks a spring of water. Who will say that this is not so, except someone who has within him what God detests—pride—as it is written in the Gospel?

Or will we entertain these proud thoughts, I saying, “Are you the one who is going to guide me?” and you saying, “Is this man the one who is going to teach me?” Yet we have not mourned over our sins so that God may not cast us away from himself on the day of our distress. Are these not people to whom he will say at that time, “Depart from me,” or, “I do not know who you are”? What will we say at that time? Will we say, “In your name we received positions of authority or greatness. In your name we clothed ourselves in habits. In your name we lived in your holy places. In your name we read the Scriptures”? Those people too will say, “In your name we prophesied, and in your name we cast out demons, and in your name we performed many miracles.” But they will gain nothing. Why? Was it because they neglected the deeds?

If he will say to these people, “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire,” because they did not do what he told them, then how much more woe to us, because we destroy necessary deeds, which are God’s judgments and what is right!

For it was because of these things that they said, “They committed sexual immorality in the thoughts of their hearts.” These are the ones whom ruin follows, as it is written: “Evil thoughts precede ruin.”
Because of these things they said, “A lying spirit stood up and dripped wine and strong drink for you.”

For those whom he has made enemies of true righteousness through these ways are countless, with their love extinguished, and with jealousy and hatred. while stealing.
It is no surprise if Christians suffer at the hands of pagans or heretics because they are jealous of them,
just as the Philistines made Isaac suffer because they were jealous of him, and just as all God's people have endured every hardship from the beginning until now because of all the godless people.
But it is all the more astonishing that we are jealous of one another, make one another suffer, and hand one another over to death, since we have one God.

There is another practice that harms the fathers and brings ruin to the children: those in authority honoring people so that they will follow them, or appointing them to necessary duties in God's service, although they hear about and know their evil deeds.

We want to know what should be done to a good person and what should be done to an evil person. Listen to what the voice says: “[?] the one who speaks the truth in his heart and does not practice deceit with his tongue.” He said, “Every wicked person is despised in his sight, but he honors those who fear the Lord.”

Who is the person, who is the priest, who fears God? Let him guard himself against the evil deeds for which the voice rebuked Eli and his sons. And he killed them in his anger because they did not stop committing their acts of sexual immorality, but also became robbers. Instead of offering first to the Lord God, they themselves took first from
the things being offered as sacrifices.

It was in connection with this that it was said, “You have honored your sons more than me, so that they receive a blessing from the first portion of every sacrifice of Israel before me.” For it is truly an outrage for servants to stretch out their hands to eat first—especially wicked servants—while their master is at the same table, before he has given them permission.
If you want to honor people or do them favors, honor them in your house. Do them favors with what belongs to you. The altar is not the place to win people over in this way.
Nor are the Lord's body and blood the means by which to do them favors. For what you are performing is a mystery, not a matter of eating and drinking.

Nor is it a place for a person to go up to just as he is: the sexually immoral man and the prostitute, the adulterer and the oppressor, the thief and the one who swears falsely—each in his own wickedness.

I have not presented them to these people as dreams. For it is our deeds that cause these words to condemn us, and it is good that they do. Will we then repent? Will we stop storing up wrath for ourselves on the day of wrath and the revelation of God's just judgment?
If evils of this kind are ours, then [?] the speaker is to blame for saying what does not exist. But if they do exist and are increasing, then those who find fault with the speaker are sinning.

For it is for Jesus' sake that we say these things—for Jesus' sake. Let us understand that the true gift a person should give his neighbor is for each person to help his brother and his companion in his troubles—not only his troubles in outward matters, but also the troubles caused by the devil's sins.

There are things that a person may vow to do, or may not vow to do, namely: keeping his bed pure; giving charity if he has the means of this life; administering justice without favoritism; observing the days of fasting according to the rules of the church; and the firstfruits.

There are deeds which, if a person does not vow to do them, he incurs no sin. For the Lord said, “Whoever is able to bear it, let him bear it.” But if he vows to do them and does not do them, woe to him! These are: remaining a virgin, taking up your cross, following God, being a priest in his house, and being a monk.
Therefore, whoever falls away from these things or turns back from them has himself become a denier and has become a pillar of salt like Lot's wife—that is, a person with no wisdom in him.

If we say, “These words are fighting against us,” who does not fight against those whom God fights against? It is his angel or his Holy Spirit who speaks through them. Or is it a small thing for a person to serve God in complete purity in his holy assemblies?
Even if you will not remain a virgin as you promised, do not become sexually debauched. Do not sleep with a male. Do not have many wives because you do not have one.

Even if you will not do deeds like those of the angels, do not do demonic deeds either. Even if the pagans will not hear of good things among you that would make them marvel, recognize that we belong to God, and understand that the Lord is great and his power is great,

then do not let them hear of evil things among you either—evil things of a kind not even found among the other nations. They are indeed children of the devil, so that not merely one or two defile God's temple and his ordinances, as it is written.
Rather, perhaps you will find one among many, or two among multitudes, who have not defiled God's temple and his ordinances, as it is written.

The same applies to the woman who says, “I am a virgin,” when she is not one. Do not have many husbands because you do not have one. If you will not make time to bear children or raise them, do not torment yourself either by bringing them down within you through many kinds of evil means before their time.
Nor should you throw them out, not knowing whether a dog or a sow will eat them, just as you have also failed to realize that fire and the worm will take possession of you.

If you will not have children at their proper time, do not hide them in secret places, or in a well or in the water, lest their souls and their bodies be hidden in the underworld and their names be covered in darkness.
For if you had not offered your face and your eyes to an unclean man, how could you have shown the devil your heart, revealing your thoughts and your reflections to him?

Have you not heard about the woman of whom it was said, “For all those before her are [?]”? Who came before whom among those who entered you to rob and plunder your soul? Was it the wicked man? Or was it Satan? For you are the one who has already seen the king. You also know who became the guide for those who took the property from the house.

If those you brought inside had been thieves or robbers, they might have left something behind. It was the demon, who is never satisfied with committing sin, who deceived you. It was he who worked sorcery against you.

You were the first to make room for him within yourself. If you had not looked out at him, you would not have met him in the manner of a prostitute, nor would he have lurked in the corners, in the streets, and around your house.

You are the one who taught him the ways of coming in and going out deceitfully. You are the one who hid him in their heart, their soul, and their thoughts, like a woman who has hidden her adulterous lover in the storerooms and
in the corners of her house.

You are the one who brought him to the place where the treasure is hidden. You are the one who pointed it out to him. Search, you foolish virgin! Go through all their possessions so that you may know what he has not taken from the things that belong to you.

Their purity is the great treasure. Prayer is the bracelets and the various rings on their hands and fingers. Their walking in freedom is the anklets on their feet. Their obedience is the earrings in their ears. Humility is the ring and the copper necklace around their neck.
Their knowledge is the ornament on their head or around their neck. Their fasts are the bridles of their body.
They are your meditations on the word of God, the lamp for your feet.
Grace is the ointment and the oil with which you anoint yourself and which you put on your head. Truth is the band that you tie around yourself. Wisdom is the cloth in which you wrap yourself.
Has he not taken all these and the other things from you? He emptied it down to the [?]. From its furnishings he took dignity, or the wholesome sense of shame in your eyes.
That woman said to her brother, “I will take hold of you and bring you into my mother's house, into the chamber of the woman who conceived me.”

Now, just as the true virgin preserves for herself all her wealth in the good deeds she has done, praying in her strength that Jesus and his Spirit may dwell within her, you have taken hold of a hostile man and brought him into your house and into your defiled chamber. You have welcomed the unclean spirit, but you have withdrawn from the holy and beloved one, the good Spirit—not because he lacks the power to save you, but because he has handed you over to the one who hates you, because you loved strangers and followed them. I loved those who sleep with you, and you increased your sexual immorality with them. You increased the number of those who are far from you, so that they dwell in your house with you.
I am speaking about the spirit of wickedness and the rulers of the world of darkness, and also the ungodly people who have become one with you—and you are with them, you poor soul.
But their God, for his part, and their Lord Jesus—you did not leave him

for yourself in their hearts and in their thoughts, as it is written. He himself, when he saw you, forgot him, and you did not fear him. He himself will sow his righteousness, and the wind will carry you away, together with all those mixed up with you. Their deeds and their [?]—a whirlwind will scatter them.

Let us stop, then, engaging in these deeds through which we stir up God's anger and wrath against us. How long, then, will we keep speaking to God hypocritically and spreading out our hands falsely before the one from whom the ugliness of our deeds is not hidden?
How long will these troubles remain on the earth because of our acts of violence and all the things that none of us wants done to him, yet we ourselves do to one another?

“Remove the sins, and I will remove the sufferings, the scourges, and the afflictions from you,” says the voice that declares, “Remove these wicked things from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness.”

How long will we disgrace ourselves on our own, disgracing ourselves and his other good things? Who can defile or profane the Lord's ordinances without first defiling himself and profaning his own deeds?

It is impossible for me to say a word without having to give an account for it. For this reason I tell you: there is a person reading the Scriptures or singing psalms of whom they say in heaven, “The one whose mouth deserves to be shut.”
There is a person in the holy places, also clothed in the honored name, of whom they say in heaven, “The enemy of God's houses, whose habit deserves to be torn.”
There is a person going to the altar and receiving the body and blood of the Lord, of whom they say in heaven, “The one whose hands and feet deserve to be cut off.”
There is a man, and there is a woman, whom people on earth consider lights in every kind of purity, of whom they say in heaven, “Look at these people, unclean in everything!”

There will certainly be a judgment between those who hear these words with sighing and weeping and those who hear them with grumbling and complaining—if indeed they do not hate the person who rebukes them.

What will this name and this habit do for us while we engage in these improper deeds? What will enrich us is this saying spoken by the prophet: “Let the coward become a fighter. Let the one who has no strength say, ‘I am strong.’” Against whom should the coward become a fighter? Or in what should he become strong?

Let him fight for the truth and for God's judgments. Let him fight against sin. Let him become strong against empty glory, hypocrisy, favoritism, and shame before people—especially rich oppressors and godless pagans.

The person who does not pay attention to his sins when he hears these words is the person who does not think about his end and the hour of his distress. The person who finds fault with the one saying these things is the person among you whose thoughts wickedness and deceit have covered over, as it is written.

Everything from which we gain no benefit at the time of our distress is a loss to our soul. What greater wisdom have those who have come here from far away gained by making inquiries or seeking judgment about goods that have been stolen?

If a person's work is to remove specks from people's eyes that are destroying their sight, how is it not foolish for him to remove the specks and leave the beams in them? I say this because, if I am here exposing people for stealing goods, or passing judgment on them, why should I not expose them because sin has stolen them, and judge them and show them the places where the enemy has hidden them—that is, defilement, uncleanness, and every sin?
The rule of this place is that we should benefit our soul, which the whole world is not worthy of. Do not let anyone come to me about a matter of this sort. I am not that kind of person.

The great prophet Moses was in the midst of the darkness and the cloud, and God spoke with him, so that none of these matters was hidden from him. Yet he never spoke like this, nor did any of the other saints: “Go to such-and-such a place, and you will find goods that have been stolen,” or, “Who took them?” That is what those who now deceive many people do, although they know nothing. Instead, they said, “Every matter will be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses,” or that the stolen goods should be found in the possession of those who took them. As the final settlement of every dispute, he said, “An oath before God shall take place between them.”

But it was said, “Every matter will be established through the mouth of two or three witnesses.” Or stolen goods are found with those who took them. The end of every dispute—he said, “An oath before God shall take place between them.”

If Samuel told Saul, “The donkeys have been found,” what does that have to do with what you say—“Such-and-such, in such-and-such a place”—and with saying who stole some goods, rather than saying, “They have been found”? Is not saying
“They have been found” a peaceful matter? What about saying, “Look, they are over there,” or, “Who took them?”

That is how those people now stir you up to acts of hostility and other troubles, as you cause disturbances in the houses of those whom they told you had taken them. You gain nothing except lies, fighting, and hatred toward one another.

But because we have spoken of concern and have heard about concern, I will add these things: may the God of all compassion make us worthy of these two things, so that we may share in them fully. They are these: may he protect the innocent among his people, and may he also set us sinners right, freeing us from every lawless act. May he not hide his face from us from today onward, from the day when we resolved in our hearts to keep his words,
so that we too may hear this encouragement.

And again, “I will establish a covenant of peace with them, and a covenant of peace shall be theirs. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever. My dwelling shall be over them.”

And again: “I will bring back the captives of Jacob, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel.” And again: “From this time onward, I will no longer leave them in that place”—he is speaking of the land of their enemies—“and I will not hide my face from them, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, says Adonai the Lord.”

I said these things knowing that you want to hear them. Rather, I remember how I saw your tears flowing over your cheeks when this least of men spoke in this way: “Did we used to mount the chair or the throne to read aloud to those who hear the word of God in his churches, or rather did we go down into graves?”

And again: “What wisdom does a shepherd have if he draws water and gives a flock of sheep a drink, but does not give his own lamb a drink? Or what about someone who has lit many lamps in the house for others, but does not light his own in his room?”
